policy.mobileCondition: width < 768 CSS pixels or primary coarse pointer
policy.canvasResolution: native device ratio; no automatic downsampling

limitations: Desktop emulation and software GPU are not physical iPhone Safari performance evidence.
Empty basemap and one shared generated image exclude real tiles, network transport and independent photo decoding.
The benchmark uses default antialias false; the application defaults to true.
Frame intervals cover camera movement; no card/list scroll or thermal/memory-pressure measurements.
Both native and adaptive variants use the current viewport scheduler, so frame comparisons isolate rendering rather than scheduler request savings.
Initial and arrival sync durations measure synchronous reconciliation, not completion of deferred photo rendering.
Missing native active identities can be detached offscreen DOM markers; they are not evidence of source data loss.
GPU identity membership comes from public source snapshots; the separate browser interaction fixture proves paint/hit behavior.
The 4 ms cold-work target includes construction and attachment, but a bounded camera/cache pass follows it.
Flags and Breadline status markers preserve native semantics and may still reach the 500-native-marker ceiling.
GPU/ratio metadata was added for the last DPR3/mapDPR2 diagnostic; earlier rows did not record these fields. The antialias metadata field was added after that run.
Working-tree source fingerprints identify the final source; the benchmark harness gained reporting-only fields and the optional map-DPR diagnostic after the main comparisons.
WebKit executable required by the installed Playwright version was unavailable; no WebKit result is claimed.
Source fingerprints describe the measured working tree; the atomic commits exclude unrelated MapCanvas hunks and apply repository formatting without changing measured behavior.
